examples.scenario: Executive impersonation via Business Email Compromise (BEC) where the attacker sends an email from a lookalike domain that closely mimics the CFO’s real domain, requesting an urgent wire transfer. The email bypasses SPF but fails DMARC, and is delivered due to partial DKIM alignment failure. The recipient’s email client shows the display name as the CFO, but the actual sender domain is suspicious. The attacker uses a recently registered domain with minor typosquatting and sophisticated subject line obfuscation to evade filtering.

DKIM signature failed validation for domain company.com
SPF passed for cf0-company.com but domain is suspicious
Email subject contains zero-width space Unicode characters
Domain was registered less than 7 days before email delivery
Email filter flagged as spam but allowed delivery due to SPF pass
No secondary verification on high-risk wire transfer request
examples.detection_method: Correlation of DMARC failures with newly observed domains resembling internal executive domains; heuristic detection of Unicode zero-width characters in subject headers; alert on wire transfer requests from external domains failing DMARC but passing SPF; employee training and enforced multi-channel verification for financial requests; monitoring domain registration feeds for lookalike domains.
